subject: Caravel AI — Incident response, RCA draft, and accountability timeline
messages:
From: Laura Rivera <laura@caravel.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Caravel AI Support <support@caravel.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: spike in latency and 5xxs impacting checkout (urgent)

Diego / Monica —

We started seeing elevated latency and a spike in 5xx errors across model endpoints used by our checkout flow starting ~08:45 PST. Impact: 30–40% increase in latency, and ~4% request error rate (mainly 503/502) for the t2-inference endpoint. This is affecting about 12% of user traffic and causing retries client-side.

Can you confirm if this is a regional capacity/backpressure issue or something on your side? We have a big launch tomorrow and need an ETA for mitigation. I can share logs — do you need anything specific?

Attached: our sample request IDs (caravel_sample_ids.txt) — I can share more if you need.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Engineering — Caravel AI

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Rivera <laura@caravel.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: spike in latency and 5xxs impacting checkout (urgent)

Laura — thanks for the flag and the sample IDs. We see the error spike correlating with an unusual burst pattern from Caravel's key across multiple pods. Immediate next steps: 

- I’ve paged on-call and appointed Markus to lead the triage.
- Please share any full request traces you have (x-request-id headers) and the time window; we’ll match on our side.
- We’ll enable additional routing to avoid the overloaded GPU pool (temporary) and roll a configuration that drops oversized prefix-lists to reduce KV cache thrash.

We expect to have an initial mitigation (routing shift + circuit throttle) within 30–45 minutes. Will update here with timestamps and any customer-visible impact.

If you authorize, we’ll upload aggregated request traces to a shared Drive folder (will be limited to request metadata and timing; we won’t store request bodies without your consent).

—Diego
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:09:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: initial findings & short-term mitigations for Caravel incident

Quick summary (initial triage):
- Root symptom: sudden ~3x burst in request concurrency with long-tail token lengths from Caravel’s prod key -> KV cache churn and increased host CPU on a subset of the west-coast GPU cluster.
- Error class: transient 502/503 from overloaded worker processes; not a model weight corruption.
- Short-term mitigations executed at 09:55 PST: traffic re-route to healthy pool (west-2), enabled per-key soft-rate limit, and increased prefetch window for KV cache on effected hosts. That reduced observed 5xxs to ~0.8% and latency approaching baseline after ~12 minutes.

Open actions (owners / ETA):
- Markus: collect heap/CPU profiles and attach aggregated logs (ETA: 11/01 14:00 PST).
- Diego: coordinate exec note + customer readout (ETA: 11/01 16:00 PST).
- Monica: confirm whether Caravel wants a postmortem with timeline + credits (ETA: 11/01 18:00 PST).
- Kimberly (SRE): validate patch that improves KV eviction policy (PR ready, ETA: 11/03).

Requesting confirmation on whether we should proactively propose a one-week usage credit for the hours impacted.

—Markus
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime Performance

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Rivera <laura@caravel.ai>, Samir Doshi <samir@caravel.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Draft RCA and proposed remediation timeline (attached)

Laura / Samir —

Apologies again for the incident last week. Attached is our draft RCA (caravel_rca_draft.pdf) and the mitigation timeline spreadsheet (mitigation-timeline.xlsx). High-level summary:

- Incident window: 2026-11-01 08:45–09:08 PST (primary impact); residual elevated latency through 09:20 as reroutes converged.
- Cause: sudden concurrency burst with atypically long prompt prefixes that exceeded our optimistic KV cache assumptions causing eviction storms on a subset of GPU hosts in west-1.
- Immediate fix: traffic reroute + soft per-key throttles + adjusted prefetch window (deployed 09:55 PST).
- Permanent actions (proposed): KV eviction policy change, model worker backpressure control, alert/threshold tuning for long-tail token distributions, and an automated per-key anomaly detector.

We’ve included an accountability timeline in the spreadsheet with owners and delivery dates. Proposed customer remediation: a pro-rated credit equivalent to one week of typical usage during the impacted window, plus a joint technical review meeting next Wednesday (11/10).

Attachments: caravel_rca_draft.pdf (RCA + timeline), aggregated-logs-1101.zip (truncated metadata only), mitigation-timeline.xlsx.

Please confirm receipt and say if you want any parts redacted before we post a finalized RCA. We can also do a live walkthrough — suggested times: 11/10 10:00–11:00 PST or 11/10 15:00–16:00 PST.

Best,
Diego

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Rivera <laura@caravel.ai>, Samir Doshi <samir@caravel.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T17:23:00-08:00
Subject: Final readout, commitments, and ownership tracker — Caravel incident (CRV-4672)

Hi all —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. This thread is the single source of truth for follow-through. Below is the agreed accountability timeline and current status:

1) Final RCA publication (redacted version made public) — Owner: Diego Fernandez — Due: 2026-11-12 — Status: In review (Diego). Link: https://redwood.app/drive/rca/caravel-CRV-4672
2) KV eviction policy change (code + canary) — Owner: Kimberly Park — Due: 2026-11-17 — Status: In progress (PR open). JIRA: INF-8934
3) Per-key anomaly detector (proto + alerting) — Owner: Markus Klein — Due: 2026-12-01 — Status: Design doc approved
4) Customer remediation (usage credit) — Owner: Monica Patel — Due: 2026-11-15 — Status: Approved (pending billing ops) — Amount: one-week pro-rated credit
5) Joint technical review (customer meeting) — Owner: Diego Fernandez — Scheduled: 2026-11-10 10:00 PST — Status: Confirmed
6) Post-release monitoring window (2 weeks) — Owner: Kimberly Park — Starts: 2026-11-18 — Status: Pending

Outstanding asks for Caravel: please confirm the credit amount you prefer (we will convert to USD and issue via your account billing) and whether you want the unredacted logs for deeper forensics. If you approve, Billing Ops and I will issue the credit by 11/15.

If there are no objections, we’ll convert the draft RCA to the public-ready version and publish the redacted report on 11/12.

Thanks again for patience. If anyone needs escalation to execs (for additional contractual concessions), please flag here; we’ve reserved an exec slot if warranted.

—Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
